title: The AI Ledger
introduction: A source-first briefing separating announced developments, unconfirmed reporting, and editorial forecasts. Confidence labels are qualitative judgments, not calibrated probabilities.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra rolls out
items.summary: OpenAI announced Terra for its API, ChatGPT Work and Codex—not Chat. Listed standard API prices are $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens.
items.whyItMatters: Teams have another deployment option; they should test quality on their own workloads instead of treating price as a capability ranking.
items.confidenceReason: Official release documentation establishes the announcement and listed terms, not independent comparative performance.
items.historicalContext: GPT-4o mini's July 2024 launch also emphasized cost-efficient deployment. Different capability classes make raw token-price comparisons misleading.

items.title: GPT-6 Rosalind Research begins a restricted rollout
items.summary: OpenAI announced a life-sciences model for approved Research customers in Work, Codex and the API. Enterprise access begins with an off-by-default, two-week Admin Preview.
items.whyItMatters: This is a specialized research rollout, not general availability or evidence of clinical effectiveness. Organizations need explicit approval.
items.confidenceReason: Primary documentation supports announced access terms. Scientific effectiveness has not been independently assessed here.
items.historicalContext: The original Rosalind announcement on April 16, 2026 also used trusted access. This extends an existing specialized-model program.

items.title: Anthropic tests AI self-assessment for misuse detection
items.summary: Anthropic reports that self-assessment identified 78% of conversations flagged by a stronger classifier and 94% of high-priority cases, at a 1% false-positive rate in its evaluation.
items.whyItMatters: The technique could make monitoring less expensive, but agreement with another classifier is not the same as verified real-world harm detection.
items.confidenceReason: High confidence in what the published research reports; results are first-party and not independently replicated here.
items.historicalContext: Constitutional AI in December 2022 used AI feedback during training. This applies an AI-supervision idea to post-response monitoring; mechanisms and evaluation targets differ.

items.title: Unconfirmed: an Anthropic model focused on user intent
items.summary: The Information reports that Anthropic is preparing a model better at interpreting users' intentions.
items.whyItMatters: A claim worth tracking, not a basis for deployment plans. No independently verified name, launch date or benchmark is established here.
items.confidenceReason: The original headline is public but the article is paywalled. A dated secondary account attributes the report to one unnamed user; repetition does not create independent corroboration.
items.historicalContext: Recent announced model releases show ongoing iteration, but launch cadence cannot validate this particular rumor or predict its timing.

items.title: Outlook: specialized AI may retain separate access gates
items.summary: Editorial inference: specialized scientific models may continue to require distinct organizational approval rather than automatically following general chatbot access.
items.whyItMatters: Research teams should distinguish general subscriptions from eligibility for specialized capabilities when planning adoption.
items.confidenceReason: Current policy and historical continuity support plausibility, not a calibrated probability or announced future commitment.
items.historicalContext: Rosalind's April trusted-access introduction and October restricted upgrade show continuity so far, not a guarantee of future policy.

charts.title: Inside the research
charts.description: Company-reported fraction of stronger-classifier flags also caught by self-assessment, at a reported 1% false-positive rate.
charts.selectionCriteria: The two headline recall figures reported together in Anthropic's October 16 research. The high-priority group is a subset, not an independent sample or a competing model.

points.label: All conversations flagged by the stronger classifier

charts.caveat: First-party evaluation, not independently replicated here. These percentages measure agreement with a stronger classifier's flags, not proven real-world harm detection. Do not sum these bars or compare them as separate model scores. The reported 1% false-positive rate has a different denominator and should be a note, not a third bar.
